desc: The Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin (IASA) is the research division Harold Puthoff established in 1985 and incorporated under EarthTech International in 1991. Its practical significance for this board is documentary: the cover page of Christopher 'Kit' Green's Defense Intelligence Reference Document, 'Clinical Medical Acute & Subacute Field Effects on Human Dermal & Neurological Tissues', carries the IASA name above the subject headings 'Translational Sciences / Forensic Medicine - Engineering Mechanics'. IASA is therefore the organisation that produced the US government's medical study of humans injured by unidentified craft. The preface of that document quotes a 'November 2007 Proposal to Analyze Probable ET Generated Specific Near-field Electromagnetic Emissions: to Puthoff/Hathaway', which dates the solicitation to nine months before the DIA's AAWSAP contract was awarded to BAASS in September 2008 and identifies the recipients by name. The document's Hypothesis One is that human injury data is sufficient 'to reverse engineer certain aspects of the Energy / Propulsion Systems'. That is the reverse-engineering premise stated in a US intelligence-sponsored document, on an IASA cover sheet, with an appendix structure built on a named case catalogue.
